page.layout: One page of text, one column of running text in roman and italic with Greek inside it. No marginal notes. Printed page number 124 at the head. Catchword "exau-" at the right below the last line.

main_text.l: Imperatoribus ante assensum Pontificis Ro-
mani, licet invitum Photium in sedem re-
stitutum fuisse, tum ab ipsis petitam a Pon-
tifice restitutionem. Id non approbat, licet
non videatur improbare. εἰ καὶ ἡ [?] [illegible,
~60 letters] Licet nostra pietas, vim Photio inferens substituerit

l.i: illum ante nos, hoc est prius quam missi a nobis

main_text.l: Legati istuc venirent. Malo tamen se, ne
status Ecclesiae integer dissipetur, reme-
dium dicit afferre ex indulgentia, qua seve-
ritas legum Ecclesiasticarum moderatur.
Non ergo probat restitutionem Photii, sed
ausum illum Imperatorum, & vim illatam
tolerat. Ubi enim necessitas fuerit, & vis,
ibi ad utilitatem Ecclesiarum Dei, qui po-
testatem habet, dispensat. Si ante literas
has Pontificis Photius receptus fuerat, &
restitutus in sedem, frustra Pontifex tot in-
culcatis adhortationibus Photii reconcilia-
tionem Imperatoribus, aliisque Praesulibus
suadet. Frustra enim quod actum est, fieri
suadetur. Et qui a tot Synodis iustas ob
causas, & ob ingentia scelera condemnatus,
expulsus, inferisque per anathema devotus
fuerat, & Christianorum nomine indignus
declaratus, & ab Oecumenico Concilio

page.notes: The Greek sentence is faint and only its opening words are partly legible; the rest is marked illegible. The Latin is clear. Long s has been normalised to s and u/v, i/j to the vowel/consonant forms as instructed. The printed "Photij" was read as "Photii".
